target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a resumed session's agent run could lose its managed worktree checkout mid-run: idle GC or a separate remover could delete the session's isolated checkout while the run was using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. It also fixes the silent counterpart, where a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran without its checkout as if it were an ordinary directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease, and agent command preparation acquires it as soon as the session cwd resolves, before any workspace-dependent step, releasing it in the run's outer cleanup. The lease retains the existing PID-tagged Git worktree lock with local reference counting, so both same-process removal paths and separate-service removers are excluded while a run is active. Admission for a cwd that belongs to a removed managed worktree now fails with `managed worktree was removed: <path>` instead of proceeding. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC or session cleanup, including when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` (67e1d43911), resolving the `WorktreeSnapshotError` conflict in `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts` in favor of the typed error from main.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/command/worktree-lease.test.ts`: 32 passed, including a new removed-path admission regression.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.worktree-race.test.ts`: 2 passed; the composed regression pauses real preparation while removal races, covering both the run-wins ordering and the removal-wins-before-admission ordering.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`: 35 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`: 102 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on all changed files: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: clean.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session's agent run must keep its managed worktree checkout while cleanup or a separate remover races it, and a session whose managed worktree was already removed must fail admission instead of silently running in a recreated ordinary directory.
Real environment tested: the production agent command preparation path and ManagedWorktreeService driven end to end on a clean AWS machine (Crabbox lease cbx_619103fb2076, c7a.xlarge), with real on-disk git repositories, real managed worktree creation, and real registry state, comparing pristine main 67e1d43911 against this patch f12f79032a on identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_619103fb2076 --shell -- "bash run.sh"`, where the script creates a session-owned worktree with a nested workspace directory, seeds the session with that cwd, admits the run through the production preparation entry point, races a separate service's non-force removal, releases the run, then removes a second worktree and attempts admission for it again.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 67e1d43911)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: false
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: false
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: false
removal after the session run ends: error: unknown active worktree: b4242765-4c49-4ddc-934d-69698e802427
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation proceeded without its managed worktree: true
preparation still points at the removed cwd: true
# AFTER (this patch f12f79032a, identical inputs)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: true
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: true
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: true
removal after the session run ends: removed
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation fails with: managed worktree was removed: /tmp/openclaw-proof-bvGt15/.openclaw/worktrees/861311bf01e8bf89/proof-removed
managed checkout recreated as ordinary directory: false
```
Observed result after fix: an admitted run holds a releasable lease backed by the live worktree lock, a separate non-force remover is rejected while the run is active and succeeds after the run ends, and admission for a removed managed path fails with a clear error instead of proceeding without its checkout.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the two racing services ran in one process on the remote machine, with cross-process protection relying on the directly verified on-disk Git worktree lock.
